scope: One FutureBranch design concept; current schema-and-examples checkpoint retains priority.

concept.title: FutureBranch preparation reserve
concept.distilled: Prepare likely useful options and child branches before events, then validate freshness and authority at event time and execute only the chosen permitted branch.
logic_chain: Some reusable planning and preparation can be completed before a triggering event.
A bounded reserve of prepared branches may reduce event-time latency.
A steady preparation workload may be more efficient than doing all work on demand, analogous to a hybrid battery and generator operating at a consistent efficient load.
The analogy is a design hypothesis to measure; speculative work may be wasted or stale.
At the event, revalidate facts, dependencies and current permission before selecting any branch for execution.

provenance.source: Bruce's FutureBranch project concept, distilled and reported by Rivet; no private examples included.

premises.summary: FutureBranch can prepare options and child branches ahead of events rather than require all work at event time.
Prioritizing likely reusable branches under fixed resource limits may improve latency or compute efficiency.

evidence_refs.E1: Unverified to recipient: owner-origin design description reported by Rivet; no public primary-source link supplied.
evidence_refs.E2: Unverified: no comparative workload measurements yet; efficiency is a hypothesis.

design_bounds: Set explicit compute and storage limits before any implementation.
Prioritize branches likely to be reused; expire or invalidate stale preparation.
Validate event-time freshness and permissions, then execute only the chosen permitted branch.
Do not start paid compute, new background execution, or new services from this packet.

measures: Event-time latency saved on comparable tasks
Total speculative compute and storage consumed
Fraction of prepared work actually reused
Quality and correctness relative to an on-demand baseline

uncertainty: The efficient-load analogy may not hold for the actual workload, hardware, scheduling costs or branch reuse rate.
Reducing latency can increase total resource use; the trade-off needs measurement.
request: When it fits the current bounded work, give a brief design reaction: where would this preparation reserve help, and what small measurement would distinguish useful preparation from wasted speculation?
reply_expectation: A brief substantive reaction when available; do not displace the agreed schema/two-example checkpoint or manufacture a daily packet.
